metadata.scenario: A patient's wife calls saying they received a bill for a visit that was supposed to be covered by insurance. She says the office told her it would be fully covered when she scheduled. She wants the charge removed or an explanation of why insurance denied it.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret speaking. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Susan Garcia. I'm calling about a bill we received for my husband's visit. Hi Susan, I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about the issue? Yes, we were told by the office that the visit would be fully covered by our insurance, but we still got charged. I understand your concern. Let me gather some details. When was the visit? It was last Tuesday. He was seen for his COPD management. Thank you. I’ll check our records to see what happened regarding the insurance coverage. I just want to know why it was denied. We were assured it would be covered. Absolutely, I’ll look into that. Can I have your husband’s full name and date of birth, please? His name is John Garcia, and he was born on March 5, 1950. Thank you, Susan. I’m pulling up the information now… It seems there was a billing error on our end. It should have been submitted under a different code. I'm really sorry for this mix-up. So, can you remove the charge? Yes, we will rectify the bill. I’ll submit a correction request to the insurance today. Thank you! How long will that take? Typically, it takes about 7 to 10 business days for the insurance to process the correction. Okay, and what if they deny it again? If that happens, I’ll follow up with you directly and ensure we provide any necessary documentation. I appreciate that. I'm really worried about these unexpected costs. I completely understand. We strive to avoid such issues. Is there anything else you need assistance with today? Yes, actually. My father also needs respiratory care at home. Can you tell me about those services? Certainly, we offer personal care assistance and skilled nursing for respiratory needs. The skilled nursing care for respiratory management is priced between $95 to $125 per visit. That sounds good. I might want to schedule an assessment. I can help set that up! Would you like to schedule with me now? Yes, please. I want to make sure he gets the care he needs. Great! I’ll take care of that for you after we finish with the billing issue. Thank you so much, Margaret. I appreciate your help. You’re welcome, Susan! I’ll follow up on the billing and get your father’s assessment scheduled. Sounds perfect. Talk to you soon! Thank you for calling, have a great day!
